blindReadings.lens: MISSION/OUTCOME — does the estate move Oak's disadvantage-gap mission, via teachers, to pupils?
blindReadings.headline: The vision's stated centre of gravity (third-order: teacher workload down, pupil-reaching quality up, disadvantage gap closing) has no execution estate beneath it; the estate is organised around the first-order delivery machine and the one live app, while the second- and third-order causal links the vision calls its strongest mission alignment sit unplanned and unmeasured.
blindReadings.vision_clarity: High and genuinely coherent on intent. VISION.md is explicit that the live Curriculum MCP server is one app and the vision is the whole infrastructure (SDK, hybrid search, graph, EEF evidence, MCP servers/Apps, reusable components, the portable Practice). The three orders of effect are well-articulated (lines 213-248) and the document itself names the third order — teacher workload reduction and widening reliable access to a high-quality curriculum to close the disadvantage gap — as "where the repository aligns most strongly with Oak's mission" (line 247). Audiences, non-goals, and the teacher-as-pedagogical-expert boundary (ADR-194) are clean. The clarity weakness is altitude honesty: the vision asserts reusability as "a first-class delivery concern, not a side effect" (lines 142-143) and rests the entire second order on the reusable component set, but those are aspirational claims the estate does not yet substantiate. The vision reads as a destination statement that the plan estate has not been re-shaped to serve.
blindReadings.value_chain_assessment: The chain breaks precisely where the vision says it matters most. First order (Oak ships safely+fast via the Practice) is over-resourced and well-grounded: practice + agent-tooling is ~39% of all docs (159 of 409). The plan estate is structured around the Curriculum MCP path-to-GA — a single app — with milestones (M2/M3) defined as that server's release states, and even those are under fresh-eyes re-assessment because "the prior definitions do not stand" (high-level-plan lines 66-70; milestones README lines 35-42). The second order (enablement via reusable infra) is the vision's load-bearing leverage claim, yet 'reusable-components build/packaging' has no execution plan — the components are enumerated in prose (VISION lines 126-140) and a partner-adoption contract is referenced, but nothing plans how they are extracted, packaged, and made adoptable. The third order (teacher→pupil outcomes) has no instrumentation: 'value-proof instrumentation' and 'pupil safeguarding/editorial-correctness' are both missing execution plans, even though the vision lists outcome indicators (teacher workload reduction, pedagogical-quality retention; lines 296-300) and explicitly gates learner-facing surfaces on a safeguarding programme that does not yet exist (lines 182-185). The result: the estate can demonstrably move the first order, but the causal bridge from delivered infrastructure to teacher value to pupil outcome is asserted, not planned and not measured.
blindReadings.action_surface_assessment: The action surface is dense but mis-weighted relative to the vision and partly unreachable. Only 28 of 409 paths are live-critical against 112 speculative and 79 stale/superseded — roughly 47% of the estate is not pulling toward live value. 149 of 355 live+future plans (42%) are unlinked from their sibling-lane README, so a large fraction of intended action is not navigable from its own collection entry point — a discoverability failure that means the plan portfolio cannot be reliably traversed to find what serves the mission. Collection organisation is weak (4 cluttered, ~8 mislaned by the census). The whole estate is gated heavily on externals (upstream-oak-api 24, elastic 17, mcp-spec-ga 13, cloudflare 12), which is appropriate for an infrastructure layer but concentrates delivery risk outside Oak's control. The seven named missing execution plans (reusable-components packaging, value-proof instrumentation, pupil safeguarding/editorial-correctness, legal/DPIA/DSAR, performance, production Clerk, ops/sustainability/funding-envelope) are not minor gaps: they are the planning homes for the second- and third-order effects plus the conditions for sustained operation. Their absence means the action surface optimises the part of the chain already strongest.
blindReadings.biggest_strategic_gap: There is no planned, instrumented bridge from delivered infrastructure to the teacher-and-pupil outcome the vision names as its strongest mission alignment. Concretely, three of the seven missing execution plans converge on one axis — value-proof instrumentation (is teacher planning workload actually reduced?), reusable-components build/packaging (the entire second-order enablement thesis, which the vision calls first-class but the estate leaves in prose), and pupil safeguarding/editorial-correctness (the protection of what reaches pupils, which the vision gates the third order on). Until the estate carries plans that (a) extract and package the reusable components for real external adoption, (b) instrument leading/outcome indicators so second- and third-order effects are observed rather than asserted, and (c) safeguard editorial correctness of what reaches pupils, the work can prove only the first order — Oak ships safely and fast — while the mission-causal claim that this closes the disadvantage gap remains unevidenced. The first-order delivery machine is being optimised; the mission outcome it exists to serve is neither planned for nor measurable.

blindReadings.lens: value-chain (where across the three orders is value CREATED vs DELIVERED)
blindReadings.headline: Value is created densest at order 1 (the Practice) and thinnest at order 3 (teacher-pupil outcomes) — the exact inverse of where the vision places mission weight; only the MCP server actually delivers order-2 value to a real consumer, and no instrumentation closes the loop back to the mission the work claims to serve.
blindReadings.vision_clarity: High clarity on WHAT is built and WHY it matters in principle; structurally weak on the value-delivery chain. The three orders (VISION.md L213-248) are asserted to magnify each other ("each magnifying the next"), but the magnification is one-directional narrative, not a traced or measured bridge. Order 1 (Practice) and order 2 (reusable infra) are described as concrete deliverables; order 3 is named as where the repo "aligns most strongly with Oak's mission" (L247) yet is explicitly held out of scope at the pupil boundary (Non-Goals L182-185). The vision is honest that pupils are reached only indirectly through teachers' tools, but it does not commit to how value-arrival at orders 2 and 3 is observed — leaving the most mission-critical link as the least specified.
blindReadings.value_chain_assessment: CREATED-vs-DELIVERED splits cleanly by order. Order 1: value both created and delivered — the Practice exists, runs, and propagates (ADR-124 "already exercised across Oak repos", VISION.md L164), and the census confirms it as the estate's centre of mass (practice docs ~39% of 409). Order 2: value abundantly CREATED (SDK, live Curriculum MCP server, search, graph-aligned surfaces, the six-item component inventory at L126-139) but DELIVERY is real only for the MCP server — the one surface reaching an external consumer. The other five components are asserted as reusable yet the census flags 'reusable-components build/packaging' as a MISSING execution plan, and the partner-adoption contract is a single sector-engagement plan; reusability is declared 'first-class' (L143) without a packaging/delivery spine. Order 3: value neither instrumented for creation nor confirmed as delivered — the census lists no 'value-proof instrumentation' and no 'pupil safeguarding/editorial-correctness' plan, while VISION.md's own outcome indicators (L297-300: 'evidence that downstream tools reduce teacher lesson-planning workload') have nothing in the estate that would produce that evidence. Net: effort-density decays toward the mission while rhetorical importance increases toward it — the chain creates value upstream and asserts, rather than measures, its arrival downstream.
blindReadings.action_surface_assessment: The actionable surface is concentrated at orders 1-2 and well-mapped: the high-level plan routes the MCP path-to-GA, observability, security, compliance, SDK/MCP, graph, and practice through owned collections with clear entry points. But the action surface has a systematic hole exactly where value is supposed to be DELIVERED and PROVEN: the census's missing-execution-plans list (value-proof instrumentation, pupil safeguarding/editorial-correctness, reusable-components packaging, legal/DPIA, performance, production Clerk, ops/funding) are all downstream-of-creation, delivery-and-proof concerns. 287 of ~409 paths carry no milestone and 42% of live+future plans are unlinked from their sibling README — so even the built surface is hard to navigate to outcomes. The milestone ladder is itself under fresh-eyes re-assessment (high-level-plan L66-70), with an impact-first redraft parked in a future stub gated on owner direction — meaning the estate currently has no settled definition of what 'delivered value' even is past M2.
blindReadings.biggest_strategic_gap: There is no value-arrival instrumentation anywhere past order 1 — the estate measures that surfaces are BUILT, never that value REACHES anyone. The vision names order-3 teacher-pupil outcomes as the strongest mission alignment and specifies outcome indicators for it (reduced planning workload, sustained pedagogical quality, external reuse growth), but the census shows zero value-proof instrumentation plans and no editorial-correctness/safeguarding plan to underwrite the one promise that touches pupils. The result: a sophisticated value-CREATION engine (orders 1-2) whose claim to mission impact (order 3) rests entirely on assertion. Until there is a delivery-and-proof spine — minimally, reuse/adoption telemetry for the MCP server and reusable components, plus an editorial-correctness gate for what reaches teachers — the three-orders story is a creation pipeline mislabelled as a value chain.

blindReadings.lens: EXECUTION/DETERMINATION — is the action surface organised to execute the strategy with clarity and resolve?
blindReadings.headline: The action surface is organised to ship one app (the Curriculum MCP server) and to perfect the means (the Practice), but it has no execution spine for the two-thirds of the vision that lives beyond that app — external enablement and pupil outcomes — and it is executing against a release ladder its own assessment says does not stand.
blindReadings.vision_clarity: Strong at the strategic surface, narrow at the execution surface. high-level-plan.md §Strategic Goal cleanly states the WHAT ("world-class primitives and modular building blocks for education applications") and names five pillars; the README's collection table and explicit reachability invariant give the estate a legible map. But the vision's three orders of effect do not survive into the action layer. Every coordinating spine — high-level-plan.md §Milestone State and the whole curriculum-mcp-path-to-ga/roadmap.md — sequences against the single MCP HTTP server. The survey corroborates: 287 of 409 docs carry no milestone, and the milestones that exist (M2/M3/M4-GA) are entirely the one app. The "whole infrastructure, not one app" framing is asserted strategically but is invisible in what the action surface actually drives.
blindReadings.value_chain_assessment: Inverted relative to the vision's stated value chain. Order-1 (Oak ships safely+fast via the Practice) is the most heavily instrumented part of the estate: agentic-engineering-enhancements + agent-tooling hold ~39% of all docs, and the two largest active artefacts are the 238KB Sentry observability plan and the 38KB comms-corpus research plan — both Practice/means work. Order-2 (enablement of Oak teams, external developers, EdTech, sector) and Order-3 (teacher-pupil outcomes) are comparatively thin: the SDK-publishing, reusable-sector-components, value-proof-instrumentation, and pupil-safeguarding/editorial-correctness work either sits in queued/future lanes or has no execution plan at all. The chain that connects the live MCP app to a measured pupil-facing outcome is not built — there is no value-proof instrumentation lane, so the third order cannot currently be observed, let alone driven.
blindReadings.action_surface_assessment: Disciplined in form, under-resolved at the decisive points. Positives, read first-hand: clear lifecycle taxonomy (future/current/active/archive), an explicit reachability invariant, a thin non-owning strategic index (roadmap.md is genuinely a map, not a second source of truth), and PDR-018 end-goal/mechanism/means framing. But three resolve gaps undercut execution. (1) The roadmap's own §4/§6 mark Privacy & compliance, Performance, and MCP-spec-GA as "No execution plan yet" and list five unauthored owner-gated paperwork items (A1-A5) — the M3 gate depends on work nobody is yet executing. (2) The milestone ladder the whole arc runs against is, per the 2026-06-15 readiness assessment, judged not to stand, yet the impact-first redraft is parked in a future/ stub gated on owner direction while execution continues against the superseded ladder. (3) The reachability invariant the README calls "structural, not cosmetic" is not actually held — 42% (149/355) of live+future plans are unlinked from their sibling lane README, so a large fraction of in-flight work is invisible to handoff and priority-setting. Determination is high on the MCP-app means; it is deferred or absent on the ends.
blindReadings.biggest_strategic_gap: There is no execution spine for the vision beyond the single live app, and no instrumentation to prove the value the vision exists to create. The action surface has a full M1→GA milestone ladder for the Curriculum MCP server but zero milestone structure for the SDK, the reusable sector components, the broader graph/evidence infrastructure, external-developer/EdTech enablement (Order-2), or pupil-facing outcomes (Order-3) — the survey's 287 no-milestone docs and the missing value-proof-instrumentation, reusable-components, and pupil-safeguarding/editorial-correctness plans confirm it. The consequence: the team can execute the MCP app to GA with full resolve and still not be organised to demonstrate that the curriculum reached teachers in their tools, that external developers were enabled, or that pupils were protected. The single highest-leverage move is to give the two beyond-the-app orders of effect their own milestone-bearing execution spine, starting with a value-proof instrumentation lane that ties the live product back to a measured teacher/pupil outcome — without it, the strategy's reason for existing is unmeasurable and therefore undriveable.

verdicts.why: VISION.md is genuinely active (last_reviewed 2026-06-12), internally coherent, and the clearest layer — that part stands. But 'does NOT need rewriting' is overstated. The same-day 2026-06-15 readiness assessment (§5.7) found 'two products conflated' (end-user vs developer surface), and K1 redefined 'live' as an observed-impact evidence state — neither is yet reflected in VISION's framing. VISION's 'How We Measure Impact' section names leading/outcome indicators but defers all operationalisation to the reports surface, and its three-orders model presents the second order (reusable components) as a delivered 'What We Deliver' inventory when the estate shows it is documentation-only (sector-engagement Phases 2-4 all 'Future'). The vision is sound and current; the claim that it needs no revision after K1-K3 is too strong.

The architecture's excellence is corroborated first-hand by the in-repo readiness report §3 ('Schema-first codegen... Strongest part of the system') and the privacy/security ADRs (160/158). So the core claim stands. But 'genuinely excellent / strongest part of the system' is overstated when applied to the whole substrate as shipped: the app README itself admits 13 of 37 tools (the aggregated set) bypass ToolExecutionResult — 'architectural debt' missing error handling, logging and type safety, which also undercuts the five-axis observability claim; graph tools return full dumps (token-inefficiency, trips host directory policy); and the privacy *legal* artefacts (DPIA/DSAR/notice) are named-but-unwritten. The design is excellent; the runtime implementation carries acknowledged debt. Excellent-in-architecture, debt-in-implementation.

Directionally well-grounded. Second order: the reusable-components inventory lives ONLY in VISION.md 'What We Deliver'; the sole sector plan (sector-reusable-components-adoption.plan.md) is an explicit documentation 'contract' with four pending todos and no implementation — its own words: 'Execution of implementation work remains owned by engineering collections'. The sector roadmap puts external-data-source demos and partner playbooks (Phases 2-4) all in 'Future'. So 'documentation-only with no execution plan' is exact. Third order (teacher experience) is the not-yet-built React MCP App rebuild, mostly current/future. The inward weighting is real (agentic-engineering-enhancements 136 + agent-tooling 73 md files are the two largest plan collections). Caveat: the precise '~39%' is method-dependent — by all plan .md files inward is ~19%, by the survey's doc-weighting it is ~39%; the ratio shifts with denominator but the skew itself is robust. The substantive claim holds.

The deepest-gap framing is right in spirit and the readiness report's K1 makes value-proof a GA precondition — but 'no plan or instrumentation measures whether ANY pillar is creating that value' is factually overstated. The observability collection IS a five-axis plan that explicitly includes a Product axis (tool_invoked + search_query emission) and a Usability axis (feedback capture, widget_session_outcome), with the Product-axis MVP plans (observability-events-workspace, search-observability) live in current/. The launch-readiness framework A1 names value-proof, release-and-observe, and a qualitative+quantitative impact bar. So instrumentation *infrastructure* exists and is partly live. The TRUE residual gap is narrower and should be stated as such: the outcome indicators (teacher-workload reduction, pedagogical-quality maintenance, sector reuse) have no operationalised measurement — the impact bar is an explicit 'open decision', usability feedback capture (L-9/L-12) is deferred to public beta, and curriculum-content-observability is a future strategic brief. 'Is it working' is under-instrumented for outcomes, not un-instrumented across the board.

Corroborated first-hand. The front-door contradiction is live and verifiable today: root README says 'Current status: Invite-Only Alpha', the app README header says 'Status: private alpha / Next status: public alpha' and '#Authentication: External access is not available', and the milestone tracker says M2 in progress — three authoritative surfaces, three answers (the readiness report §2 flagged exactly this). Planning discipline genuinely IS sound: plans/README.md documents an explicit reachability invariant (root -> collection -> lifecycle -> plan), a four-lane lifecycle taxonomy, and update rules. So the drift is behavioural (estate grew faster than curation), not a design flaw. The 1095 plan .md files (435 .plan.md, 248 archived) make the curation-vs-growth tension concrete. Claim holds.

Two distinct sub-claims with different fates. (a) 'External long-poles have no owned timelines' is TRUE but the upstream-Oak-API case is misframed as a defect: upstream-feature-requests/README.md states by design 'this repository must not edit those upstream repos... Each upstream team's canonical intake owns implementation' — requests are recorded with Status/Priority and handed over. No owned timeline is the correct posture for another team's repo, not allocation-by-gravity; the genuine gap is the absence of a *risk/contingency register* for those dependencies, not a missing timeline this repo could own. (b) 'Inward/outward allocation happened by gravity, not a conscious owner decision' is partly contradicted by the evidence: the owner has an explicit priority sequence (comms research first, then roadmap) and took ratified keystone decisions K1-K3 on 2026-06-15. Determination/under-resourcing of outward pillars is real, but framing the whole allocation as unconscious overlooks the conscious decisions on record.

refutations.missing_from_synthesis: The six claims, taken together, omit four things a holistic view must include. (1) The repo ALREADY HOLDS this diagnosis. The 2026-06-15 readiness assessment and launch-readiness framework independently re-derive C2 (provenance/architecture strongest), C3 (engineering-shaped estate has no home for what matters), C4 (no value-proof gate anywhere — 'the most load-bearing gate'), C6 (no owned cost/safety owners), and a full impact-first milestone re-ladder. The synthesis presents as fresh findings what the estate has already named and owner-ratified (K1-K3). A holistic view states the real question is execution-of-a-known-plan, not discovery of a blind spot — and credits the self-correction loop that produced these artefacts as itself the strongest evidence the Practice (first order) works. (2) SAFEGUARDING / pupil-boundary content safety. The readiness report calls this 'the largest gap'; none of the six claims mention it. For a children's-education AI product whose brand travels into an unobservable host LLM, the absence of a safeguarding owner, harm-response runbook, and editorial-correctness accountability is a more acute mission risk than the inward/outward plan skew. (3) STATUTORY obligations as a public body — UK GDPR/DPIA/DSAR, the ICO Children's Code, and public-sector accessibility duties (the org's own WCAG 2.2 AA bar) are legal floors, not roadmap items; legal artefacts are named-but-unwritten. (4) The MCP product is NOT a public product today (its own README: 'External access is not available'), the upstream key is unlimited (no cost ceiling), and Cloudflare volumetric defence is unpromoted — so the live-now operational/financial exposure is omitted by claims that focus on plan-estate shape. The synthesis is an accurate map of the planning corpus but under-weights the live product-safety, legal, and operational realities that the in-repo readiness work already surfaces.

verdicts.why: VISION.md is current (last_reviewed 2026-06-12, confirmed first-hand) and structurally sound, so 'no rewrite needed' largely holds. But 'clearest layer / cannot dent it' is overstated: the vision carries internal tensions the survey itself names and I confirmed. (1) school-data-search has ZERO vision anchor (grep returns nothing) yet is a live queued collection — the vision does not account for a real workstream. (2) The 'How We Measure Impact' section is aspirational ('impact SHOULD be tracked'; values 'live in the reports surface and high-level plan') but those surfaces carry no actual measurement (see C4) — the vision asserts a measurement posture the estate does not honour, which is a vision-to-reality gap, not pure clarity. (3) VISION §191 claims graph capabilities are 'live today' while HLP §123 calls the EEF tool 'the live first proper graph tool' and a 2026-06-09 readiness report treated graph tools as in-progress — reconcilable (anchored relationship tools are live, confirmed via MCP) but the 'live today' framing sits at the optimistic edge. 'Soundest layer' is fair; 'clearest and undentable' is not.

The substrate IS real and strong: schema-first codegen packages exist (oak-sdk-codegen, oak-curriculum-sdk, oak-search-sdk, graph-corpus-sdk), 489 test files give high density, the production MCP responds 200 first-hand, and the readiness assessment independently rates provenance/codegen/privacy(ADR-160)/security(ADR-158) sound. But 'genuinely excellent — strongest part' is dented at the most load-bearing point: I code-confirmed that the 13 aggregated tools bypass ToolExecutionResult (return Promise<CallToolResult> directly), and these 13 are NOT peripheral — they are the FLAGSHIP surface (search, fetch, get-curriculum-model, all four graph tools, get-eef-evidence, browse-curriculum). The README itself labels this 'architectural debt' missing error handling, logging, and type safety, and it directly undercuts the 'full five-axis observability' claim because the most-used tools do not route through the instrumented path. Also confirmed first-hand: the shared upstream key is unlimited (limit:0/remaining:0/reset:0) so there is no cost ceiling, and Cloudflare (the volumetric defence) is unpromoted in future/. 'Excellent engine' is true for the generated/typed core; the claim overstates by treating the flagship tool path and the security/cost envelope as already excellent.

Confirmed first-hand. Practice weight: aee + agent-tooling are the two largest collections and the survey's 159/409 (~39%) is corroborated by the reachability spot-check showing aee/current alone holds 54 plan docs dominated by Practice openers and specialist-capability clones. Second order: the sector-reusable-components plan explicitly states 'Execution of implementation work remains owned by engineering collections' and its own todos are all documentation/contract work (cross-links, adopter profile, supported-vs-experimental matrix, playbook scaffold) — there is NO packaging/publish execution plan; a literal search for packaging/publish-component plans returns only the adoption contract plus unrelated engineering plans. Third order: the only outcome-facing plan is eef-outcome-evaluation-infrastructure, which is future-status and narrowly scoped to whether EEF caveats survive LLM mediation — not teacher-experience build nor workload/adoption proof. So 'engine superbly, orders-closest-to-mission under-invested' stands. Minor nuance (not enough to downgrade): the inward 39% is partly defensible because the first-order Practice IS a named vision pillar and a shipped reusable component, so 'under-invest' should be read as relative skew, which is exactly how C3 frames it.

This is the most robust claim. VISION 'How We Measure Impact' names leading indicators (adoption/downloads/active integrations, delivery throughput) and outcome indicators (teacher-workload reduction, pedagogical quality maintained, ecosystem reuse), and says values 'live in the reports surface and the high-level plan' — but no plan or instrumentation actually populates them. A search for value-proof/impact-instrumentation execution plans returns only a readiness FRAMEWORK (type: readiness-framework, not executable), a future STUB (launch-readiness-and-milestone-redefinition), and the future EEF evaluation harness — none is a live instrumentation plan, and all are MCP-app- or EEF-scoped, not ecosystem-wide. The survey's own gap-analysis and the readiness assessment §5 independently agree value-proof has no estate home. The readiness K1 even inverts 'live' to require proven impact, making the absence of instrumentation a precondition gap, not a post-launch nicety. 'Is it working?' is genuinely assumed, not evidenced, across all pillars.

Verified first-hand. Reachability: I reproduced aee/current at EXACTLY 23 linked / 31 unlinked (literal-filename presence test), matching the survey's 31/54 precisely after I caught and corrected my own initial miscount — the substring method is sound, not inflated. The 31 unlinked are dominated by session *-opener.md files and *-specialist-capability clones, directly confirming 'the drift is behavioural / hygiene, not architectural' and 'estate grew faster than curated.' Strategic indexes: the high-level-plan was refreshed to 2026-06-15 (now carries the fresh-eyes readiness pointer), so the 'indexes do not carry live intent' point was true at survey time but is being actively cured — a slight time-sensitivity, not a refutation. Planning discipline (ADR-117/PDR-018) sound while product lanes stay clean: corroborated — the unreachable residue concentrates in high-churn practice lanes, not the product collections. Claim stands.

Two of three sub-claims stand: (a) the outward pillars ARE under-resourced relative to mission centrality (confirmed via C3/C4); (b) external long-poles have no owned timelines — confirmed first-hand: the Cloudflare gate is unpromoted in future/, dated 2026-04-28, explicitly 'strategic context only,' with no execution dates or owner, and production Clerk is research-only with the 'shared vs independent instance' question open. The upstream-Oak-API dependency is real (the upstream-feature-requests collection exists; 51 plan docs reference the upstream API), though '24-plan' is the survey's external-gate bucket, not independently re-counted by me. BUT the framing 'allocation happened by gravity, not a conscious owner decision' is wrong on the evidence: the owner holds an explicit, dated, recently-revised priority sequence (set 2026-06-12, superseding 2026-04-22) whose live queue is (1) comms-research follow-ons, (2) naming v3, (3-5) Sentry/PostHog observability, (6) integrate the oak-api repo — a CONSCIOUS, inward-weighted sequence. The inward tilt is therefore at least partly a deliberate owner choice, not drift-by-gravity. C6 mistakes a deliberate (if arguably mission-suboptimal) sequencing decision for an unconscious one. 'Determination is the missing verb' is rhetorically overstated where an owner sequence demonstrably exists; the sharper true claim is that the sequence prioritises inward work over the mission-closest outward pillars — a contestable priority, not an absence of decision.

refutations.missing_from_synthesis: The six claims are internally coherent but share a blind spot: they critique the estate's SHAPE and never test whether the SHIPPED PRODUCT creates value, and they omit several load-bearing realities. (1) WHO holds authority. The synthesis treats K1-K3 and the impact-first ladder as settled; the survey itself (§12) corrects that these are an AGENT's claim, NOT a verified owner decision. A holistic view must flag that the entire 'impact-first redraft' the claims lean on is an unratified proposal — the milestones have not actually been rewritten. (2) The PRODUCT IS LIVE AND USABLE. None of the six claims credits that the production MCP server responds (200), serves real grounded curriculum + EEF + four graph tools today, and is consumed in ChatGPT/Claude — the third-order channel is thin in PLANNING but partially REAL in PRODUCTION. The claims over-index on the plan estate as if it were the only evidence of value delivery. (3) SAFEGUARDING / pupil-boundary safety is the single largest gap the readiness assessment names (no editorial-correctness owner, no harm-response runbook, AI-hallucination-attributed-to-Oak risk) and it is MORE mission-critical than proof-of-value, yet C4 elevates proof-of-value as 'the deepest gap.' A holistic view ranks pupil-safety above measurement. (4) COST / SUSTAINABILITY: the unlimited shared upstream key means no cost ceiling for a publicly-funded body — a live operational exposure today, absent from all six claims. (5) DEPENDENCY DIRECTION: the deepest external risk is that the whole stack is downstream of an Oak API owned by ANOTHER team (shared unlimited key, upstream versioning) — a structural single point of failure the claims mention only as a counting bucket. (6) WHAT 'EXCELLENT' COSTS: the claims praise the Practice (39% of plans) without asking whether that inward investment is itself the value-proof gap's cause — the team has instrumented HOW IT BUILDS far more than WHETHER WHAT IT BUILT HELPS ANYONE, and that is the real synthesis: the estate measures its own engineering reflexively but has no mirror pointed at the teacher or pupil.

verdicts.why: VISION.md is genuinely current (last_reviewed: 2026-06-12) and is the most internally-consistent layer, so 'clear and sound' stands. But 'does NOT need rewriting' is too strong against the repo's own freshest evidence. The 2026-06-15 readiness assessment (.agent/reports/mcp-app-live-product-readiness-assessment-2026-06-15.md, owner-ratified K1-K3) lands a structural correction the VISION does not yet reflect: VISION's 'How We Measure Impact' frames value-proof as medium-term OUTCOME indicators tracked post-investment, whereas K1 inverts this to make value-proof a PRECONDITION of GA. VISION also still implies the repo serves three co-equal groups (developers, agents, teacher-products) while K2 narrows the primary audience to teachers/curriculum leaders. The doc is sound but already one owner-decision behind; 'no rewrite needed' is a claim the 2026-06-15 record contradicts.

The substrate genuinely exists and is built, not aspirational: packages/sdks/oak-sdk-codegen (with vocab-gen), packages/core/graph-core (with dist), apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http, apps/oak-search-cli. ADR-160 redaction barrier and ADR-158 security architecture are real, and the 2026-06-15 assessment independently calls schema-first codegen 'the strongest part of the system.' So the core of C2 stands. But 'genuinely excellent / strongest part' is overstated as a blanket: the app's OWN README (apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/README.md L354-362) admits 13 of 37 tools bypass ToolExecutionResult — missing error handling, logging, and type safety — and labels it 'architectural debt'; the assessment notes this directly undercuts the five-axis observability claim (you cannot observe what does not route through the instrumented path). The substrate is strong AND carries a known third-of-surface integrity hole; 'excellent' should be qualified, not absolute.

Verified quantitatively and qualitatively. The inward weight is if anything understated: by .plan.md files, agentic-engineering-enhancements (69) + agent-tooling (52) = 121 of 270 = 45% (survey said ~39% on a whole-file denominator of 209/539, which is the conservative read). Third-order thinness confirmed: M2 milestone (.agent/milestones/m2-extension-surfaces.md) progression gates are entirely engineering/infra with no teacher-facing or value gate. The substance stands: no current/active plan or live instrumentation measures whether any pillar creates value. M2's gates are pure engineering hygiene; the observability 'product' axis grep returned no teacher-workload/adoption/reuse-signal measurement; the only genuine value-measurement plan (sector-engagement/eef/future/eef-outcome-evaluation-infrastructure.plan.md) sits in future/ and defers even the DECISION of whether teacher-trust/workload measurement belongs there. But 'assumed, not evidenced' overstates the unawareness: the gap is now NAMED and owner-ratified, not invisible. The 2026-06-15 assessment K1 elevates value-proof to a GA precondition ('Live = real users demonstrating positive impact'), §8.2 calls 'no value-proof gate, anywhere' the ladder's most load-bearing missing gate, and §10.3 makes 'define the Stage-3 impact bar' an explicit next step. Both halves verified. Drift: ~539 non-archive plan files (1095 with archive); 181 future/ + 180 current/ + only 35 active/, i.e. the estate is overwhelmingly queued/deferred relative to in-flight work; many dated 2026-02 to 2026-04 snagging/evidence files still sit in current/ lanes (e.g. oak-preview-mcp-snagging-2026-04-23, trinity-...-2026-04-29). Strategic-intent carriage is weak: only 8 plans link VISION.md. Discipline is genuinely sound and not the cause: ADR-117 (plan-templates-and-components) and PDR-018-planning-discipline.md both exist and define the reachability invariant and lifecycle taxonomy (.agent/plans/README.md). So C5's framing — good rules, behavioural drift because the estate grew faster than curation — is accurate. The 42% precise figure I could not exactly reproduce (it depends on the survey's denominator/linker), but the directional claim of large-scale unreachability/burial is well-supported by the lifecycle skew and the vision-link sparsity.

The structural facts hold. The 24-plan upstream-Oak-API dependency is real and owned by another team with no owned timeline: .agent/plans/upstream-feature-requests/ is classified 'Reference + coordination' and the plans/README states requests are 'recorded here and handed over' — i.e. raised and passed to the Oak Open Curriculum API team, with no return ETA. External long-poles (elastic, cloudflare, mcp-spec-ga, ontology-repo, clerk) likewise appear as gates without owned dates. The under-resourcing of outward pillars is corroborated by C3's verified inward skew and the documentation-only second order. 'Determination is the missing verb' and 'allocation by gravity not conscious decision' are the one genuinely interpretive (rhetorical) part — they are a reasonable reading of the evidence rather than a stated fact, but the underlying allocation imbalance and the absence of owned outward timelines are factual and verified.

refutations.missing_from_synthesis: The six claims describe shape/altitude problems (inward skew, proof gap, estate drift, missing determination) but OMIT the acute, already-documented facts that a holistic view must lead with — most of which the repo's own 2026-06-15 readiness assessment already recorded, meaning this synthesis partly re-derives an existing verdict rather than adding to it. Specifically missing: (1) The 'live product' framing is false today on the repo's own words — apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/README.md says 'Status: private alpha', 'External access is not available', Clerk TEST instance, internal-Oak-only; the synthesis treats the MCP server as the live product without noting it is not externally available. (2) The front-door contradiction — three authoritative surfaces (app README, milestone tracker, continuity) disagree on the current stage (private alpha vs M1-complete/M2-in-progress vs EEF-live); a product whose canonical README contradicts its own tracker cannot launch, and no claim mentions this. (3) SAFEGUARDING / pupil-boundary content-safety is, per the assessment, 'the largest gap' — an AI product whose output reaches children, with no harm-response runbook, no editorial-correctness owner, no safeguarding sign-off; C4 reduces this to generic 'proof of value' and loses the child-safety specificity (the safety boundary is the pupil, not the adult user). (4) Legal/regulatory exposure for a PUBLIC BODY is statutory not optional — UK GDPR/DPIA/DSAR, the ICO Children's Code, public-sector accessibility duties, host-directory T&Cs — all named-but-unwritten; none of the six claims name the legal/compliance void. (5) Operations & sustainability — no cost ceiling (unlimited upstream key + unbounded serverless + ES), no support/on-call/status-page/alerting-before-launch, no funding envelope for a publicly-funded body; the SLO plan is circularly gated '30 days post-launch.' (6) Missing OWNERS, not just missing plans: editorial/curriculum-correctness, safeguarding, DPO, accountability, single go/no-go owner — the determination gap (C6) is really an accountability/ownership gap. (7) The milestone ladder itself is already assessed as not standing (it is an auth-posture progression masquerading as a product ladder); C5 critiques the plan estate but not the milestone spine that sits above it. A holistic view leads with: it is internally-gated, not live; it is unsafe-by-omission at the pupil boundary and unlawful-by-omission for a public body until the legal/safeguarding/ops payload is built and owned — and value-proof is the gate that forces all of that to be true before GA.
